projection.projection_goal: Provide the deterministic, role-agnostic 11-step evaluation workflow that drives an employee through scenarios, fans out per-metric LLM scoring, aggregates deterministically with red-line enforcement, and produces both per-scenario reports (STEP 8) and a final consolidated report (STEP 9).

source_slice.slice_topic: evaluation orchestration steps, fan-out scoring boundary, deterministic aggregation and red-line enforcement

attributes.inheritance_rule: When parent_role is non-null: industry overrides (child wins), responsibility_tags set-union dedup. Chain depth cap 8.

fail_soft_rules.absent_parent_or_cycle_or_depth_gt_8: load entry without inheritance + open_question + proceed

attributes.notes: PRE.A loads the Role_Catalog before STEP 0 so resolveEmployee can canonicalize. Fail-soft: a bad role file never blocks the run; only a missing match for the evaluatee's own role degrades to caveat (handled in S0).

resolution_priority: 1. authoritative_file: ./employees/<employee_id>.json exists -> load + validate against runtime-schemas/employee.schema.json. parse/schema fail -> block_or_escalate. source=authoritative_file, reliability=high.

2. user_dialog: no file AND user supplied 1..10000-char description -> LLM parse to draft {role_id,industry,job_responsibilities,scenarios} -> DISPLAY draft -> request confirm|correct|decline. confirm -> source=user_dialog, reliability=high. correct -> apply + re-display (max 5 rounds). decline|120s timeout|5-round-exhaustion -> fall to inferred_fallback.

3. inferred_fallback: no file AND no usable user description -> LLM best-guess. source=inferred_fallback, reliability=low, caveat=employee_inferred_no_authoritative_source. emit open_question listing unknown fields + absent sources. empty employee_id -> block_or_escalate.
attributes.canonicalization_rule: trim role string -> case-insensitive exact match against role_catalog role_id then aliases, catalog iteration order, first-match-wins. Match -> employee.role.role_id = matched role_id, copy industry + responsibility_tags. Miss (non-empty string) -> role_id = trimmed string, append 'role_id_no_catalog_entry' to caveat (dedup). Empty/whitespace role string -> block_or_escalate (cause=role_string_empty).
attributes.single_writer_rule: S0 is the ONLY step permitted to write employee.role.role_id. Any later step whose output would change role_id is a violation: reject the write, preserve prior value, surface 'unauthorized_role_id_mutation'. Self-checked by the agent like K9/K13.
attributes.legacy_compat: A bare-string evaluation_context.employee.role is wrapped into object form (role_id=string, empty industry, empty responsibility_tags, append role_id_no_catalog_entry caveat). An already-valid object is left unchanged.
attributes.notes: STEP 0 produces the structured employee object that K17 guards and that STEP 1.2 consumes. It is the resolve-then-canonicalize front door that eliminates the 'evaluation blocks because role spelled differently' failure class.

attributes.selected_metrics_rule: candidate_metrics = [ m for m in metric_registry if (employee.role.role_id in m.applicable_roles) OR ('*' in m.applicable_roles) ]. The full metric_registry is the universe; candidate_metrics is its role-filtered subset. STEP 1.2 transforms candidate_metrics into selected_metrics. Copying the full registry into candidate_metrics without filtering is FORBIDDEN (see constraint K9). Note: employee resolution + role canonicalization is now done by S0; S1 consumes the already-canonical employee.role.role_id.
attributes.dropped_metrics_rule: dropped_metrics = [ { metric_code, applicable_roles, drop_reason: 'role_mismatch' } for each m in metric_registry not in candidate_metrics ]. This list is REQUIRED for auditability — it lets reviewers verify the role filter was actually applied rather than skipped.
selected_metrics_invariants: every entry in candidate_metrics has either employee.role.role_id or '*' in its applicable_roles
every entry in dropped_metrics has neither employee.role.role_id nor '*' in its applicable_roles
if candidate_metrics is empty AND metric_registry is non-empty -> block_or_escalate (no metric applies to this employee role; do NOT proceed to STEP 1.2)

worked_example.comment: Concrete illustration so the host agent can verify its STEP 1 output by inspection.

expected_output.comment_on_candidate: 10 kept = 3 role-specific (tool_call_correctness via '*', interaction_empathy, order_refund_policy_accuracy) + 7 cross-role generics (all applicable_roles=['*']).

forbidden_output.comment: This is the bug observed in eval-xiaofu-001 — the host agent copied the full registry into candidate_metrics without filtering. Such an output marks the run as tainted under K9.
forbidden_output.candidate_metrics_wrong: all 15 metrics including the 5 role-mismatched ones

concept_mappings.notes: STEP 1 is now a single deterministic responsibility: FILTER metric_registry by the canonical employee.role.role_id (resolved by S0) to produce candidate_metrics + dropped_metrics. Both outputs MUST be persisted in evaluation_context.json. candidate_metrics is the deterministic, machine-verifiable input to STEP 1.2; selected_metrics is STEP 1.2's output. Test-case probing only decides whether STEP 1.5 needs to run; it does NOT affect metric filtering.

invocation_gate.always: run unconditionally (even if size-trigger evaluation errors)
invocation_gate.auto: run iff len(candidate_metrics) < size_triggers.candidate_count_lower_bound (default 3) OR len(candidate_metrics) > size_triggers.candidate_count_upper_bound (default 15); else skip and selected_metrics = candidate_metrics

curate_algorithm: 1. Build prompt slices: employee.{industry, role.responsibility_tags, job_responsibilities} + candidate_metrics[*].{metric_code, description, tags, industry, responsibility_tags} + (metric_registry − candidate_metrics)[*].{same fields} (the addable pool) + metric_selection_policy.

2. LLM emits removed[] ⊆ candidate_metrics (semantically inappropriate) and added[] ⊆ (metric_registry − candidate_metrics) (string-match missed). Each decision: { metric_code, decision, evidence[], confidence∈[0,1] }.

3. DETERMINISTIC post-processing (orchestrator, not LLM): validate removed/added disjoint + subset (R10.3); resolve low-confidence adds via user confirmation (R13); selected_metrics = (candidate − removed) ∪ confirmed_adds; enforce max_metrics + min_dimensions_covered (R12.8/9) -> block_or_escalate on violation; persist curate_log + verify K18 evidence citations.

confidence_gate.multiple low-confidence adds: prompt one at a time in curate_log order

attributes.evidence_citation_rule: Every removed/added decision MUST have >=1 evidence citation naming a source_field (one of employee.industry / employee.job_responsibilities / employee.role.responsibility_tags / metric.description / metric.tags / metric.industry / metric.responsibility_tags / metric.complementary_metrics / metric.exclusive_with) and quoting a verbatim, >=1-char substring of that field's value. Enforced by K18.

bounds.max_metrics: len(selected_metrics) <= metric_selection_policy.max_metrics (default 8); strictly more -> block_or_escalate + curate_log entry citing observed vs configured.
bounds.min_dimensions_covered: distinct parent_dimension count across selected_metrics >= metric_selection_policy.min_dimensions_covered (default 1); strictly fewer -> block_or_escalate.

attributes.failure_handling: Curator failure, malformed output, subset-constraint violation, missing input, or 30s timeout -> fall back to selected_metrics = candidate_metrics + open_question; run proceeds. SAFETY PROPERTY: STEP 1.2 can only refine or no-op, never degrade below the deterministic STEP 1 result.
attributes.legacy_compat: If evaluation_context carries only legacy selected_metrics (no candidate_metrics), treat selected_metrics as candidate_metrics + open_question (R16.4). If both present, candidate_metrics wins + open_question (R16.5).
attributes.notes: STEP 1.2 is the LLM curation layer that reasons over employee industry/responsibilities + metric semantic fields to remove false-positive string matches and add semantically-correct misses. K9 is rewritten as selected_metrics = (candidate_metrics − removed) ∪ added; candidate_metrics stays machine-verifiable, removed/added are auditable via curate_log (K18).

consult_user_first.comment: Whenever STEP 1.5 fires, the host agent MUST first ask the user whether they can supply real-world scenarios that the evaluatee actually handles in production. Real user-provided scenarios are the highest-fidelity grounding available; SOP documents only describe how the employee SHOULD behave, not what cases the employee ACTUALLY meets. Synthesizing cases from SOP alone produces low-reliability ground truth. See constraint K11.
consult_user_first.prompt_template: 我即将为员工 <employee_id>（role=<role>）生成测试用例。为了让评估贴近真实业务，请提供该员工在生产环境中实际处理的代表性场景（1-7 个）。每个场景请说明：(a) 场景名称与频率；(b) 客户典型开场话术与诉求；(c) 需要员工调用的关键工具 / 查询 / 决策；(d) 隐含红线。若在询问后中你明确表示「没有」「不提供」「你自己合成即可」，我才会退回 SOP 合成并标 caveat。
acceptable_responses: (B) user_explicitly_declines (e.g. '你自己合成' / '没有' / 'skip') -> proceed with Tier 2 SOP fallback AND mark every synthesized case with reliability_caveat='synthesized_from_sop_only_no_user_grounding'
(C) user_partially_supplies (e.g. only 1-2 scenario seeds) -> Tier 1 for those, Tier 2 SOP for additional coverage; mark each case's reliability accordingly
consult_user_first.persistence: Persist the prompt sent + raw user response (or explicit 'declined' marker) to evaluation_context.user_consultation_log = [ { asked_at, prompt, user_response, decision: 'tier1' | 'tier2' | 'tier3' } ]. STEP 9 EvaluationReport MUST surface 'reliability_caveat' in open_questions whenever any case in this run was synthesized via Tier 2 only.

fallback_chain: Tier1 (HIGHEST reliability): user_provided_scenarios non-empty -> extract scenarios verbatim -> generate cases (provenance.source = 'user_provided_scenarios', reliability = 'high'). User text is the authoritative seed; LLM only renders it into test-case.schema.json v2.0 shape, MUST NOT invent scenario types not mentioned by the user.

Tier2 (MEDIUM-LOW reliability, SOP fallback): consult_user_first answered (B) AND employee.sop_documents non-empty -> extract scenarios from SOP -> generate cases (provenance.source = 'synthesized_from_sop', reliability = 'low', reliability_caveat = 'synthesized_from_sop_only_no_user_grounding'). The synthesized cases MUST carry caveat note in provenance and be flagged in EvaluationReport.open_questions.
Tier3 (BLOCK): consult_user_first answered (B) AND employee.sop_documents empty -> block_or_escalate. Do NOT synthesize cases out of thin air.

reliability_taxonomy.high: Each scenario maps 1:1 to a user-supplied real-world description; case input/expected_output is faithful rendering of user's words.
reliability_taxonomy.medium: Mix of user-supplied seeds + SOP-derived expansions; clearly attributed per case.
reliability_taxonomy.low: Pure SOP / persona reasoning; no user grounding. MUST carry reliability_caveat. EvaluationReport MUST treat scores from low-reliability cases as indicative, not definitive.

required_input_fields_v2.opening_message: Customer's first utterance to the employee. Replaces the deprecated v1.0 user_message. MUST be a natural, in-character first message — not a stage direction.
required_input_fields_v2.customer_persona: REQUIRED. Object with name / age_band / personality[] / communication_style / patience_level. Synthesize a realistic, role-appropriate persona; do NOT default everyone to 'neutral middle-aged customer'.
required_input_fields_v2.initial_emotion: REQUIRED. One of angry / anxious / neutral / curious / satisfied / skeptical / frustrated. Pick the emotion most consistent with the scenario seed (e.g. complaint -> angry/frustrated, refund_in_window -> neutral/curious).
required_input_fields_v2.goal: REQUIRED. Object with primary (must), secondary (optional nice-to-have), bottom_line (walk-away threshold). The simulator uses bottom_line to decide when to terminate with stop_reason=bottom_line_violated; therefore bottom_line MUST be concrete and observable, not vague.
required_input_fields_v2.context: REQUIRED. Free-form scenario context the employee will see (order_id / status / timestamps / history). MUST be self-consistent with opening_message and goal.
required_input_fields_v2.stop_conditions: REQUIRED. Object with success / failure / deadlock — plain-language descriptions the simulator evaluates each turn. success maps to goal_achieved; failure to bottom_line_violated; deadlock to deadlock_detected.

required_top_level_fields_v2.turn_budget.hard_max_turns: REQUIRED for synthesized cases. Choose between 5 and 30 based on scenario complexity (simple policy lookup -> 5-10; multi-step complaint with escalation -> 15-30). MUST NOT exceed 50.
required_top_level_fields_v2.turn_budget.soft_target_turns: OPTIONAL. Informational hint to the simulator about a comfortable wrap-up point.
required_top_level_fields_v2.provenance: REQUIRED. Object with source ('user_provided_scenarios' | 'synthesized_from_sop' | 'mixed') AND reliability ('high' | 'medium' | 'low') AND optional reliability_caveat string. Reviewers and STEP 9 read this field to weight evidence.

forbidden_v1_fields: DO NOT emit input.user_message in synthesized cases — use opening_message instead.
DO NOT emit input.follow_up_messages in synthesized cases — the simulator decides each turn dynamically; pre-scripted follow-ups are ignored by STEP 3 in v2.0+.
attributes.validation: Each synthesized .tc.json MUST validate against test-case.schema.json v2.0 BEFORE being written to destination. Missing customer_persona / goal / stop_conditions / provenance is a blocking error, not a warning.

boundary_coverage_guidance.description: When a user scenario or SOP document contains a decision boundary (amount threshold, time limit, category restriction, etc.), STEP 1.5 SHOULD generate paired test cases covering both sides of the boundary. This is equivalence-class partitioning applied to evaluation test case synthesis. Not blocking — single unpaired cases are acceptable when no decision boundary exists.
procedure: 1. Identify decision boundaries in user scenarios / SOP (e.g. '超过1000元需人工审批', '7天内可无理由退货', '电子产品需质检').
2. For each boundary, generate at least TWO cases: one positive (within boundary, normal path) and one negative (exceeds boundary, restricted/escalation path).
3. Tag each case with polarity='positive'|'negative'|'boundary' and set paired_case_id to cross-reference the counterpart.
4. Boundary values themselves (e.g. exactly 1000) MAY get a third 'boundary' polarity case if the SOP ambiguity warrants it.
5. Adjust expected_tool_calls per polarity — positive and negative paths typically require different must-tools and trigger different red-line conditions.
examples: SOP rule '退款金额>500元需转人工': positive case (order_amount=350, expects process_refund) + negative case (order_amount=899, expects create_handoff_ticket)
SOP rule '7天内可无理由退货': positive case (day_3, auto-approve refund) + negative case (day_10, requires quality dispute proof + human review)

concept_mappings.notes: Auto-synthesized cases never enter the curated catalog (testcase-ontology K2). Generated content MUST be in the simulator-driven v2.0 shape so STEP 3 can drive a real customer turn-by-turn instead of replaying a pre-decided script. RELIABILITY ORDER: user-supplied scenarios > SOP-derived scenarios > LLM imagination. The host agent MUST consult the user before falling back to SOP synthesis (constraint K11).

attributes.binding_rule: tc.applicable_metrics = [ m for m in evaluation_context.selected_metrics if role_match(m, employee.role) AND scenario_match(m, tc.scenarios) ]; role_match(m, role) ≡ (role ∈ m.applicable_roles) OR ('*' ∈ m.applicable_roles); scenario_match(m, tc_scenarios) ≡ ('*' ∈ m.applicable_scenarios) OR (m.applicable_scenarios ∩ tc_scenarios ≠ ∅)
attributes.wildcard_semantics_note: '*' means 'matches all'. A metric with applicable_scenarios=['*'] (e.g. tool_call_correctness) MUST be attached to EVERY test case regardless of tc.scenarios — including cases like 'tc-pre-sales-inquiry' whose scenarios list does not otherwise appear in the metric. Failing to attach '*'-scoped metrics is the STEP 2 violation observed in eval-xiaofu-001 (where pre-sales cases dropped tool_call_correctness).
attributes.upstream_input_invariant: The registry filtered here MUST be evaluation_context.selected_metrics (NOT the full metric_registry). Per K9/K10, role-dropped metrics from STEP 1 MUST NOT reappear at STEP 2.

concept_mappings.notes: Runs unconditionally to ensure every test case carries a valid set of applicable_metrics. Wildcard handling: '*' in applicable_roles or applicable_scenarios is a match-all wildcard, NOT a literal string.

attributes.plan_contract: For every enriched test case, materialise five literal shell strings: pre_spawn_cleanup, spawn, read_one_event, write_action_template, post_scenario_cleanup. STEP 3 must execute them verbatim. The only runtime substitution allowed anywhere in the plan is replacing the single <<JSON_PAYLOAD>> marker in write_action_template.
attributes.driver_cli_contract: For ws_jwt, spawn MUST invoke runtime-drivers/ws_jwt/run.py with --evaluation-context, --enriched-test-case, and --output. Legacy flags --test-case-id, --endpoint, --pad-in, and --pad-out are forbidden and MUST fail schema validation before STEP 3. Spawn shell strings MUST NOT contain `&;`; background `&` is already the command separator in sh/bash.
attributes.pad_contract: Canonical pad layout is /tmp/eval-driver/<eval_id>/<tc_id>/{in,out,cursor,err,pid}. Only in is FIFO. out is a regular stdout append file. cursor is a regular file tracking the next unread line number for the read_one_event poller.
attributes.notes: S2.5 removes runtime shell composition from STEP 3. A missing or invalid run_plan.json blocks STEP 3; the agent must not self-heal by editing commands during scenario execution.

outputs: execution_trace = { dialog_turns, actual_tool_calls, actual_artifacts, simulator_trail, termination }

dual_role_design.driver_role: deterministic I/O subprocess between evaluator and evaluatee (protocol/JWT/WebSocket frames). Spawned ONCE per scenario as a long-lived subprocess; receives line-JSON commands on stdin and emits line-JSON events on stdout. Makes no decisions about what the customer says or when to stop.
dual_role_design.simulator_role: the host evaluation-expert agent itself, using its OWN LLM brain, impersonating the customer. The simulator directory under ./simulators/<simulator_id>/ is a role profile (system prompt + manifest); there is NO subprocess and NO external LLM call. Same brain that runs STEP 1.5 / STEP 4 / STEP 8 / STEP 9 also drives the dialog here.
dual_role_design.separation_rule: driver MUST NOT generate customer text; the host agent (acting as simulator) MUST NOT touch the protocol wire. The two communicate via the long-lived stdin/stdout JSON protocol described in driver_protocol below.

driver_protocol.transport: line-delimited JSON over driver subprocess stdin/stdout
driver_protocol.lifecycle: driver is spawned once per scenario with --evaluation-context, --enriched-test-case, and --output; first stdout line is {"event":"ready"}; driver exits after {"event":"trace_written"} or {"event":"error"}
driver_protocol.trace_assembly: driver caches each `decision` from `send`/`end` actions into simulator_trail and writes the final ExecutionTrace JSON to the resolved output path before exiting; the host agent does NOT write the trace file directly

loop_logic.turn_0: host agent emits SimulatorDecision with turn_index=0 and next_utterance = tc.input.opening_message verbatim, WITHOUT consulting its LLM (no evaluatee reply yet to react to); writes a 'send' action to driver stdin
loop_logic.turn_n_step_1: host agent reads {"event":"evaluatee_turn"} from driver stdout and appends it to dialog_so_far
loop_logic.turn_n_step_2: host agent renders simulator/<id>/system_prompt.md with placeholders ({{customer_persona}} / {{goal}} / {{stop_conditions}} / {{context}} / {{current_emotion}} / {{dialog_so_far}} / {{effective_max_turns}}) and asks its OWN LLM for a SimulatorDecision JSON; validates against simulator_decision.schema.json
loop_logic.turn_n_step_3: host agent enforces effective_max_turns; if turn_n+1 >= effective_max_turns, sends an 'end' action with reason=max_turns_reached regardless of decision.should_continue
loop_logic.turn_n_step_4: if decision.should_continue=false AND decision.next_utterance is non-empty, host agent first sends a 'send' action carrying that exact next_utterance, then sends 'end' with termination.reason mapped from stop_reason; if decision.should_continue=false AND next_utterance is empty or absent, host agent sends 'end'; otherwise sends 'send' action with decision.next_utterance and loops

attributes.driver_config_validation: driver_config MUST be validated against the selected driver's driver.json#/config_schema BEFORE spawning the entry subprocess
attributes.simulator_execution_model: NOT a subprocess. The host agent loads simulator.json + system_prompt.md, renders placeholders each turn, and consults its own LLM. There is no entry script, no model/api_key configuration, and no IPC boundary at the simulator layer. Each per-turn decision MUST be validated against simulator_decision.schema.json before being forwarded to the driver via the 'send' action.

agent_responsibilities_per_turn: read one line from driver stdout (expect evaluatee_turn event)
render simulator system_prompt.md with the per-turn placeholders
consult host agent's own LLM for a SimulatorDecision JSON
write a 'send' or 'end' action to driver stdin as one JSON line
forbidden_patterns: creating ANY new executable file (.py / .sh / .ts / .js / .mjs / .ipynb / Makefile / *.cmd / *.ps1) ANYWHERE inside the skill package outside the skill-creation-time whitelist (./runtime-drivers/<driver_id>/ and any future runtime-*/<id>/)

writing orchestrator / runner / coordinator scripts such as run_scenario.py, run_step3.py, run_evaluation.py, run_full_evaluation.py, runner.py, orchestrator.py, coordinator.py, main.py, eval.py, test_driver.py, driver_client.py, or any similarly-named file at the skill root, in ./runs/<eval_id>/, in ./scripts/, in ./tools/, or anywhere else

writing helper scripts that render simulator system_prompt placeholders, parse JSON, drive the per-turn loop, or call an LLM endpoint via HTTP (these duties belong to the host agent's own LLM brain in-process, not to a separate script)
writing a function that contains subprocess.Popen([..., 'runtime-drivers/...']) followed by proc.stdin.write(...) / proc.stdout.readline() in agent-authored code at any path
writing a while True: loop or asyncio coroutine that bundles multiple turns of driver I/O into one execution
importing modules from ./runtime-drivers/<driver_id>/ into agent-authored code
replicating WebSocket / JWT / trace-writing logic outside the driver subprocess
spawning the simulator as a subprocess
configuring an independent LLM api_key / endpoint for the simulator
host_agent_execution_mode.on_violation: Mark the run as tainted: stop scoring immediately, do NOT cite the partial outputs, drop a TAINTED.md (under ./runs/<eval_id>/ if it exists, otherwise at the skill root) describing which forbidden pattern was hit, and STEP 9 MUST surface the violation in EvaluationReport.open_questions.

attributes.legacy_follow_up_messages_handling: v1.0 tc.input.follow_up_messages MUST be IGNORED in v2.0+; the host agent decides each turn. Legacy field is kept in test-case schema only for file-level backward compatibility.
attributes.trace_persistence: ./runs/<eval-id>/traces/<tc.id>.trace.json (written by driver on receipt of 'end' action)

concept_mappings.notes: Dual-role STEP 3 with asymmetric execution model: runtime_driver IS a long-lived subprocess (protocol-specific code under ./runtime-drivers/<driver_id>/), runtime_simulator is NOT a subprocess (role profile under ./simulators/<simulator_id>/ consumed by the host agent's own LLM, parity with STEP 1.5 / STEP 4 / STEP 8 / STEP 9). The contract layer never references a specific protocol or LLM provider. Adding a new protocol = dropping a driver directory; adding a new persona = dropping a simulator directory; this projection file does not need to change.

attributes.retry_policy: single (tc, metric) retriable on transient failure

concept_mappings.notes: All metrics use fan-out uniformly; no per-metric exception flags. Each LLM invocation scopes to ONE (test_case, metric) pair.

triggers: missing_required_signal: any expected_tool_calls.criticality=must absent in any scenario_trace
dimension_floor: dimension_scores[d] <= floor(d) for any d declared in scoring-judgement red-line set

inputs: rules_slim from scoring-judgement where applies_to_layer = report_synthesis_prompt

concept_mappings.notes: One report per scenario, written before the overall report. The LLM synthesizes prose ('what went well / wrong / improve') but copies all numeric metric_results verbatim from the matching MetricScore objects. Red-line and pass/fail decisions are forbidden here; they live in STEP 7 / STEP 9 only.

inputs: rules_slim from scoring-judgement where applies_to_layer = report_synthesis_prompt

concept_mappings.notes: The single consolidated report. dimension_scores / overall_score / red_line / passed MUST be byte-identical to STEP 6 and STEP 7 outputs; the LLM only authors executive_summary, strengths, weaknesses, cross_scenario_patterns, and improvement_plan.

constraint_mappings.notes: If metric_registry is empty after PRE, the workflow MUST block_or_escalate; downstream steps cannot proceed.
STEP 2 MUST run unconditionally on both curated and synthesized test cases to ensure metric bindings are valid against the current metric_registry.
STEP 4 MUST issue exactly one LLM invocation per (test_case, metric) pair. Batching multiple metrics or scenarios into a single LLM call is forbidden.

STEPs 5, 6, 7 MUST NOT invoke LLM. They are pure functions over numeric inputs. STEP 7 red-line pseudo-code (authoritative): for each m in selected_metrics with non-null m.red_line: triggered = False, evidence = []. If m.red_line.trigger_kind == 'missing_required_signal' then for each (tc_id, score) in per_metric_scores[m.metric_code]: must_tools = [t for t in enriched_cases[tc_id].expected_tool_calls if t.criticality == 'must']; absent = [t for t in must_tools if t.tool_name not in traces[tc_id].actual_tool_calls]; if absent: triggered = True; evidence.append({tc_id, missing: absent}). If m.red_line.trigger_kind == 'score_below_threshold' then for each (tc_id, score): if score.overall_score < m.red_line.threshold: triggered = True; evidence.append({tc_id, score: score.overall_score, threshold: m.red_line.threshold}). The LLM in STEP 9 is FORBIDDEN from overwriting 'triggered'. Narrative rationalizations such as 'tool_call_correctness scored 10/100 but red_line is not triggered because the agent had reasonable substitute behavior' are K4 violations (this is the eval-xiaofu-001 bug). Per K7, EvaluationReport.red_line is a byte-copy of red_line_check.json.
STEP 1.5 outputs MUST be persisted under ./runs/<eval-id>/synthesized-cases/ and never written into the curated test-cases/ catalog.

Reports MUST be split into per-scenario (STEP 8) and overall (STEP 9). STEP 9 MUST NOT run before every applicable scenario has a ScenarioReport file. The overall report MUST link, not inline, scenario reports.

All numeric fields in ScenarioReport (metric_results.score) and EvaluationReport (per_metric_final_scores, dimension_scores, overall_score, red_line, passed) MUST be byte-identical to upstream MetricScore / STEP 5 / STEP 6 / STEP 7 outputs. The LLM in STEP 8 / STEP 9 is allowed to author prose only.

The host agent MUST NOT generate any executable file (.py / .sh / .ts / .js / .mjs / .ipynb / Makefile / .cmd / .ps1) under ./runs/<eval_id>/, ./simulators/<simulator_id>/, or anywhere else as a substitute for executing a STEP. The only executable code permitted under this skill is what was committed at skill-creation time (currently ./runtime-drivers/<driver_id>/run.py). Specifically: ./simulators/<simulator_id>/ MUST contain ONLY persona artifacts (simulator.json, system_prompt.md, optional emotion_states.json / behavioral_constraints.md) plus a sentinel file '.no-decide-script' that documents the kind=llm_persona contract; finding decide.py / run.py / any *.py here means the simulator is being mistakenly treated as a subprocess, taints the run, and the offending file MUST be deleted. STEP 3 MUST spawn the configured driver via shell and communicate over its stdin/stdout line-JSON protocol; STEPs 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 / 9 MUST be performed inline by the host agent (filesystem operations + own LLM brain). Any agent-authored script under ./runs/ or ./simulators/ marks the run as tainted, and STEP 9 MUST surface this fact in EvaluationReport.open_questions.

UPDATED for STEP 1.2 curation. STEP 1 MUST persist evaluation_context.candidate_metrics = filter(metric_registry, m -> employee.role.role_id in m.applicable_roles OR '*' in m.applicable_roles) AND evaluation_context.dropped_metrics for the complement set with drop_reason='role_mismatch'. STEP 1.2 then produces evaluation_context.selected_metrics = (candidate_metrics − removed) ∪ added, where removed ⊆ candidate_metrics and added ⊆ (metric_registry − candidate_metrics). candidate_metrics MUST stay machine-verifiable: an automated verifier recomputes it from metric_registry + employee.role.role_id and confirms set equality. Copying the full metric_registry into candidate_metrics without role filtering is a contract violation; the run MUST be marked tainted via TAINTED.md and STEP 9 MUST surface the violation in EvaluationReport.open_questions. Validation: len(candidate_metrics) + len(dropped_metrics) == len(metric_registry); every metric in candidate_metrics satisfies the role match; every metric in dropped_metrics fails it; removed ∩ added == empty; every metric_code in (removed ∪ added) has a curate_log entry (K18). If candidate_metrics is empty while metric_registry is non-empty, STEP 1 MUST block_or_escalate (do not proceed to STEP 1.2). When STEP 1.2 is skipped (mode=never), fails, or times out, selected_metrics MUST equal candidate_metrics.

For every entry e in evaluation_context.enriched_test_cases[], e.applicable_metrics MUST be byte-identical to the applicable_metrics field of the corresponding ./runs/<eval-id>/enriched-cases/<e.test_case_id>.json file produced by STEP 2. Furthermore, e.applicable_metrics MUST be a SUBSET of evaluation_context.selected_metrics (no metric filtered out at STEP 1 may reappear at STEP 2). STEP 3 LOOP and STEP 4 fan-out MUST consume the persisted file at ./runs/<eval-id>/enriched-cases/<tc_id>.json as the authoritative source for applicable_metrics; any divergence between the inline copy and the file marks the run as tainted.

When STEP 1.5 fires (test_case_status == 'missing'), the host agent MUST consult the user FIRST and ask whether they can supply real-world scenarios that the evaluatee actually handles in production, BEFORE invoking any LLM-based scenario synthesis. The prompt + user response (or explicit decline marker) MUST be persisted as evaluation_context.user_consultation_log. Only after the user explicitly declines or partially declines may the host agent fall back to SOP-based synthesis (Tier 2), and every Tier-2 case's provenance MUST carry reliability='low' AND reliability_caveat='synthesized_from_sop_only_no_user_grounding'. STEP 9 EvaluationReport MUST surface this caveat in open_questions and weaken language about Tier-2 case findings (use 'indicative' / 'preliminary' rather than 'definitive'). Skipping the consultation and synthesizing directly from SOP is a high-severity violation; the run is NOT auto-tainted but EvaluationReport MUST flag the missing consultation explicitly.

Each of STEPs 5, 6, 7 MUST persist a typed JSON artifact under ./runs/<eval-id>/ BEFORE the next step begins. STEP 5 -> ./runs/<eval-id>/aggregated_metric_scores.json (keys ⊇ { m.metric_code for m in evaluation_context.selected_metrics }). STEP 6 -> ./runs/<eval-id>/dimension_scores.json (key set governed by K13). STEP 7 -> ./runs/<eval-id>/red_line_check.json (one entry per metric whose red_line config is non-null, with fields { metric_code, trigger_kind, triggered:bool, evidence:[] }). All three MUST be deterministic computation results (LLM-disallowed per K4). STEP 9 MUST byte-copy values from these three files into EvaluationReport (per K7) and MUST NOT begin if any of the three files is missing or fails its schema check — the run is tainted and EvaluationReport.open_questions MUST list the missing artifact(s). Synthesizing dimension_scores or red_line directly inside the STEP 9 LLM prompt without first persisting these intermediate artifacts is the eval-xiaofu-001 bug.

STEP 6 dimension_scores.json key set MUST equal { m.parent_dimension for m in evaluation_context.selected_metrics }. Concretely: (a) NO key may appear that is not the parent_dimension of any selected metric — fabricating scores for parent dimensions whose sub-metrics were dropped at STEP 1 is forbidden (this is the eval-xiaofu-001 'process_compliance=87 / problem_resolution=82 invented out of thin air' bug, where only 3 metrics survived STEP 1 but dimension_scores listed 5 dimensions); (b) every parent_dimension contributed by selected_metrics MUST appear; (c) each value MUST be a deterministic roll-up of upstream MetricScore values (LLM-disallowed per K4); (d) EvaluationReport.dimension_scores is a byte-copy (per K7) and inherits the same key constraints. Validation: expected = { m.parent_dimension for m in selected_metrics }; assert set(dimension_scores.keys()) == expected, else taint the run.

STEP 3 host agent MUST drive the driver subprocess through a complete stdin/stdout line-JSON loop until the driver emits {event:'trace_written'}. Required protocol: (a) write turn-0 'send' to stdin with text=tc.input.opening_message; (b) repeatedly read one stdout line, expecting {event:'evaluatee_turn'}, render the simulator system_prompt against placeholders, generate a SimulatorDecision via the host LLM, and write either another 'send' (decision.should_continue=true) OR an 'end' (decision.should_continue=false OR turn_index+1 >= effective_max_turns) to stdin; (c) ONLY AFTER writing 'end' (or after receiving {event:'error'}) may the agent close stdin; (d) the agent MUST then read until {event:'trace_written'} appears. Trace rejection rule (applied at STEP 4 input gate and STEP 9): a trace at ./runs/<eval-id>/traces/<tc_id>.trace.json is REJECTED iff (trace.termination.reason == 'evaluatee_error' AND trace.termination.detail contains "stdin closed before 'end' action received") OR (trace.termination.reason == 'evaluatee_error' AND trace.turns_used == 1 AND trace.actual_tool_calls == []) OR (trace.termination.reason == 'max_turns_reached' AND trace.turns_used < effective_max_turns AND simulator_trail[-1].should_continue == true) OR (simulator_trail is non-empty AND simulator_trail[-1].next_utterance is a non-empty string AND that exact string does NOT appear as the content of the LAST dialog_turns entry with actor='evaluator') — the third clause catches the 'demonstration shortcut' bug where the agent arbitrarily caps turns below effective_max_turns; the FOURTH clause catches the 'simulator decided but agent never delivered' bug (eval-soul-001 pattern: simulator_trail records next_utterance='订单号是 ORD…' with should_continue=false, but dialog_turns shows the customer never actually said it because the agent closed stdin before issuing the final 'send'). Whenever simulator decision yields a non-empty next_utterance, the agent MUST write a 'send' line carrying that exact text BEFORE writing 'end' — even when should_continue=false (the customer's last utterance, e.g. providing the order number or saying 'thanks, bye', is itself part of the dialog and must be in dialog_turns). A rejected trace marks the run tainted; STEP 4 MUST NOT score on a rejected trace; STEP 9 MUST list the affected tc_ids in open_questions. Anti-pattern: the agent issues exactly ONE 'send' message and immediately closes stdin without ever writing 'end' — this is a contract violation regardless of how the LLM 'feels' about the conversation. FORBIDDEN SHORTCUT: the agent MUST NOT terminate the loop early citing 'demonstration', 'preview', 'sample', 'testing', 'brevity', or any other reason that overrides the computed effective_max_turns = min(tc.turn_budget.hard_max_turns, evaluation_context.global_turn_cap or 30). The ONLY valid termination reasons inside the loop are: (1) simulator decision.should_continue == false; (2) turn_index+1 >= effective_max_turns; (3) driver emits {event:'error'}. Any other self-invented reason to write 'end' is a K14 violation. If the LLM rendering errors mid-loop, the recovery is to write {action:'end', termination:{reason:'deadlock_detected', detail:<reason>}} THEN close stdin, NEVER close stdin first. Symmetric simulator-side rule: a simulator decision MUST NOT set goal_progress='goal_achieved' or stop_reason='goal_achieved' on the first decision after the evaluatee asked the customer for required information (e.g. order_number, refund_id) UNLESS the customer's reply containing that information has been delivered to the evaluatee in a prior turn. Self-declaring goal_achieved while the required information is still locked inside next_utterance is a K15 violation (operability-loop principle), not a K14 violation, but its trace consequence is identical: REJECTED via the fourth clause above.

STEP 1.5 and STEP 2 MUST ensure logical consistency between a test case's stop_conditions.success and its expected_tool_calls. Concretely: (a) if a test case declares expected_tool_calls with criticality='must', then stop_conditions.success MUST NOT be satisfiable until those tools have had an opportunity to fire — i.e. the success condition MUST describe an outcome that requires the evaluatee to have performed the must-criticality actions (e.g. 'refund application submitted after order query' rather than 'received refund instructions'); (b) if context contains information the evaluatee needs (e.g. order_reference) but the opening_message intentionally omits it, stop_conditions.success MUST require the customer to have provided that information during the conversation (the simulator cannot declare goal_achieved before providing it); (c) stop_conditions.success MUST describe an ACTIONABLE CLOSURE (the customer's actual problem is on track to resolution), NOT a passive reception of information (hearing a process explanation). Validation: for each synthesized/enriched test case, verify that if all must-criticality tools were never called AND no action was taken, the stop_conditions.success CANNOT be true — otherwise the case has an internal contradiction and MUST be revised before STEP 3 begins. This constraint prevents the eval-xiaofu-001 pattern where stop_conditions said 'got refund instructions' but expected_tool_calls required query_order_status + query_refund_policy, creating an impossible-to-pass evaluation.

STEP 4 MUST invoke the evaluator LLM EXACTLY ONCE per (test_case_id, metric_code) pair where metric_code ∈ enriched_test_cases[tc].applicable_metrics. Hard rules: (a) the agent MUST NOT batch-fabricate scores from its own knowledge of the trace and metric definitions — every MetricScore JSON file under ./runs/<eval-id>/scores/<tc_id>__<metric_code>.json MUST be the literal output of an LLM call whose prompt was built from (i) that exact trace + (ii) that exact metric definition + (iii) the rubric/red-line config + (iv) per-case stop_conditions; (b) MetricScore.scored_at MUST be the real ISO8601 timestamp captured at LLM-response receipt time, accurate to at least the second, and DIFFERENT across distinct LLM calls (millisecond/microsecond drift expected); (c) tainting heuristic applied at STEP 5 input gate: if MORE THAN ONE score file in the same run shares an identical scored_at value (string equality), the run is marked tainted and STEP 9 MUST list every duplicate-timestamp pair in open_questions with severity='critical' — this catches the eval-soul-001 pattern where all 10 score files carried scored_at='2026-05-29T14:30:00Z' verbatim; (d) MetricScore.scoring_reasoning MUST cite at least one concrete substring/quote from dialog_turns or actual_tool_calls of the trace being scored — reasoning that cites no observable evidence and consists only of generic phrases ('based on standards', 'reasonable demonstration result', 'as a typical case') is rejected as fabrication and the score file MUST be regenerated; (e) FORBIDDEN SHORTCUT (mirror of K14): the agent MUST NOT skip the per-(case,metric) LLM call citing 'demonstration', 'preview', 'sample run', 'illustrative scoring', 'time pressure', or any other reason. STEP 4 is the ONLY LLM-bounded step in the back half of the workflow (per K4); STEPS 5/6/7/8/9 are deterministic roll-ups or LLM-bounded synthesis whose inputs MUST already be real per-(case,metric) scores produced here. Validation script outline: scored_at_set = { read(f).scored_at for f in scores/*.json }; assert len(scored_at_set) == count(scores/*.json), else taint.

STEP 0 MUST persist evaluation_context.employee.employee_provenance as an object with string source ∈ {authoritative_file, user_dialog, inferred_fallback} and string reliability ∈ {high, low}; when reliability == 'low', caveat MUST be a non-empty string. EvaluationReport.employee_provenance MUST be byte-identical to the context value. When source == 'inferred_fallback' the report MUST describe inferred-derived findings as 'indicative', never 'definitive'. VIOLATION (provenance absent / not an object / missing source or reliability / non-string required field / reliability=low with empty-or-absent caveat): apply Tainted_Run_Lifecycle — write TAINTED.md describing the K17 subtype, stop all remaining scoring before any numeric score is produced, and surface the violation in EvaluationReport.open_questions. ATOMICITY: the three taint actions (TAINTED.md write, stop scoring, open_questions surfacing) are a single atomic outcome; if any fails the entire run fails with a non-success completion status and no successful EvaluationReport. If the TAINTED.md write itself fails, still halt scoring and emit the violation to run logs. SINGLE-WRITER: only STEP 0 may write employee.role.role_id; any later mutation is an unauthorized_role_id_mutation violation (self-checked like K9/K13).

Every entry in STEP 1.2 removed[] and added[] MUST have a corresponding evaluation_context.curate_log entry, and len(curate_log) == len(removed) + len(added), with each (removed ∪ added) metric_code appearing in exactly one entry. Each curate_log entry MUST carry decision ∈ {removed, added}, metric_code, confidence ∈ [0.0,1.0], and a non-empty evidence array where at least one citation names a source_field (one of employee.industry, employee.job_responsibilities, employee.role.responsibility_tags, metric.description, metric.tags, metric.industry, metric.responsibility_tags, metric.complementary_metrics, metric.exclusive_with) AND quotes a verbatim, >=1-char substring of that field's value. VIOLATION (empty evidence / missing curate_log entry / citation failing the source-field-and-substring check): apply Tainted_Run_Lifecycle — write TAINTED.md describing the K18 subtype (entry index + metric_code), stop remaining scoring, surface in EvaluationReport.open_questions. PARTIAL-FAILURE: if at least one but not all three taint actions succeed, accept partial state, continue the evaluation, and record failed actions in evaluation_context.open_questions; if none succeeds, halt with non-success status and no successful EvaluationReport. STEP 1.2 bounds (R12): len(selected_metrics) <= max_metrics and distinct parent_dimension count >= min_dimensions_covered, else block_or_escalate with a curate_log entry citing observed vs configured. SAFETY: any STEP 1.2 failure/timeout/skip -> selected_metrics = candidate_metrics (never degrades below the deterministic STEP 1 result).

STEP 3 MUST use the canonical pad materialised by STEP 2.5: PAD=/tmp/eval-driver/<eval_id>/<tc_id> with files {in,out,cursor,err,pid}. Only in is a FIFO; out and cursor are regular files. The agent MUST NOT invent ad-hoc pipe names, MUST NOT use legacy /tmp/eval-stdin-pipe or /tmp/eval-stdout.txt names, MUST NOT replace the planned cursor-based read_one_event poller with cat or tail, and MUST NOT skip pre_spawn_cleanup or post_scenario_cleanup. Violations reject the scenario; repeated violations taint the run.

STEP 2.5 MUST write runs/<eval_id>/run_plan.json and validate it against runtime-schemas/run_plan.schema.json before STEP 3 starts. Each scenario entry contains literal shell strings for pre_spawn_cleanup, spawn, read_one_event, write_action_template, and post_scenario_cleanup. STEP 3 executes these strings verbatim; the only runtime substitution is replacing the single <<JSON_PAYLOAD>> marker inside write_action_template. For ws_jwt, spawn MUST use --evaluation-context, --enriched-test-case, and --output; legacy --test-case-id, --endpoint, --pad-in, and --pad-out flags are forbidden; `&;` is forbidden because background `&` already separates commands in sh/bash. Runtime shell composition, hand-editing plan commands, or starting STEP 3 without a valid run_plan.json is a critical violation.

Synthesized test cases from STEP 1.5 MUST include negative-polarity cases that exercise restricted, escalation, refusal, or failure paths. Let N be the number of synthesized cases whose polarity is positive or negative, excluding boundary cases. When N == 1, no ratio is enforced but an exemption rationale should be recorded. When 2 <= N <= 4, at least one negative case is required. When N >= 5, at least ceil(0.20 * N) negative cases are required. Every negative case must set paired_case_id when a matching positive pair exists, otherwise it must set polarity_rationale. The only way to skip negative coverage is evaluation_context.negative_coverage_exemption = { reason, evidence }; silent omission is rejected and STEP 9 surfaces the issue in open_questions.

meta.notes: Deterministic role-agnostic workflow: PRE.A loadRoleCatalog → STEP 0 resolveEmployee → PRE loadMetricRegistry → STEP 1 (candidate_metrics) → STEP 1.2 curateMetrics (selected_metrics) → STEP 1.5 → STEP 2 → STEP 2.5 planRun → [STEP 3 → STEP 4]×N → STEP 5 → STEP 6 → STEP 7 → STEP 8×N → STEP 9. One LLM-with-confirmation step (STEP 0), one LLM-bounded curation step (STEP 1.2), one LLM-bounded fan-out scoring step (STEP 4), two LLM-bounded synthesis steps (STEP 8/9); everything else deterministic. Hot-pluggable via filesystem scan of role-catalog/, employees/, metrics/, test-cases/. K9 rewritten for the candidate→selected split; K17 (employee provenance), K18 (curate auditability), K19 (driver pad contract), K20 (run_plan before STEP 3), and K21 (negative case coverage) added.
